evidence: Internal review suggests improving onboarding guidance for database relations.
Design team recommends improving empty states during onboarding to better explain core concepts.
Onboarding assumes users already understand database concepts.

insight.title: New users need clearer guidance on database concepts
insight.summary: Several signals point to an onboarding gap around databases and relations. New users are expected to understand these concepts before the product has explained them.
insight.recommended_action: Introduce a guided database setup with contextual explanations for relations, supported by clearer empty states.
insight.success_metric: Increase completion of the database onboarding flow and reduce help requests about database relations.
risks: Additional guidance may slow experienced users
Examples may not cover every database workflow
Completion alone may not prove understanding

evidence: The editor becomes noticeably slow when working with large pages containing many blocks.
Editor performance degrades noticeably when pages include many embedded databases.

insight.title: Large pages create a noticeable editor performance problem
insight.summary: Customers report slower editing when pages contain many blocks or embedded databases. The pattern suggests page complexity is affecting core editor responsiveness.
insight.recommended_action: Profile large-page editing and prioritize rendering improvements for blocks and embedded databases.
insight.success_metric: Reduce median input latency and page-load time for pages with many blocks or embedded databases.
risks: Optimizing synthetic large pages may miss real workflows
Rendering changes could introduce visual regressions
Performance may vary substantially by device

evidence: QA identified performance degradation in workspaces with more than 100 collaborators.
Workspace performance slows down significantly once a team reaches a certain size.
Workspace performance degrades as more members are added.
Workspace sync can take a long time after logging in.
Workspace performance slows down during peak collaboration hours.
Workspace load times increase as more integrations are added.

insight.title: Growing workspaces face compounding performance and sync delays
insight.summary: Performance degrades as workspaces add members, integrations, and concurrent activity. Slow loading and post-login sync make the issue especially visible to enterprise teams.
insight.recommended_action: Benchmark large workspaces, then target the highest-cost loading, sync, and collaboration paths.
insight.success_metric: Reduce p95 workspace load and sync time for large, integration-heavy workspaces.
risks: A single benchmark may not represent enterprise configurations
Backend improvements may not address perceived frontend latency
Peak-hour behavior may be difficult to reproduce

evidence: Design review notes that the editor toolbar feels overcrowded and hard to scan.
Custom commands or keyboard shortcuts (e.g., templated formatting) would speed workflows.
Ability to set filters in relation properties so only relevant items show up.
During testing, pages with many nested blocks occasionally fail to save changes.
Ability to filter and show more properties when adding to relation fields.
QA testing found intermittent save failures when editing large documents.
Dynamically filtering relation suggestions would save time and reduce manual work.
It’s hard to understand how databases relate to each other when building more complex workflows.

insight.title: Complex editing workflows need greater clarity and reliability
insight.summary: The evidence combines workflow friction in relation-heavy editing with reliability problems on large documents. Users need faster ways to navigate complex edits without risking lost changes.
insight.recommended_action: Prioritize save reliability first, then simplify relation controls and shortcuts for frequent editing tasks.
insight.success_metric: Reduce save failures on large documents and time required to complete relation-filtering tasks.
risks: The cluster combines several distinct editor problems
Simplifying controls may hide advanced functionality
Reliability fixes may require deeper architectural work

evidence: QA testing reveals delayed updates when multiple users edit the same page concurrently.
Collaboration feels messy when multiple people edit the same page at the same time.
Collaboration can feel chaotic when multiple people edit the same page simultaneously.
Collaboration gets confusing when multiple people edit a page simultaneously.

insight.title: Concurrent editing lacks timely feedback and coordination cues
insight.summary: Delayed updates and unclear collaborator activity make simultaneous editing feel chaotic. Users cannot confidently tell what changed or whether their view is current.
insight.recommended_action: Improve update latency and add clearer presence and change indicators during concurrent editing.
insight.success_metric: Reduce synchronization delay and collaboration-related confusion reported during multi-user editing sessions.
risks: More presence indicators could add visual noise
Network conditions may dominate perceived latency
Collaboration behavior varies by team size

evidence: Mobile editing feels limited compared to desktop, especially for database-heavy pages.
Mobile editing feels limited compared to desktop, especially for databases.
Mobile UI does not support all editor features available on desktop.

insight.title: Mobile editing falls short for database-heavy workflows
insight.summary: Customers see a clear feature gap between mobile and desktop editing. The limitation is most noticeable on pages that depend heavily on databases.
insight.recommended_action: Identify the highest-value missing database actions and bring those workflows to mobile first.
insight.success_metric: Increase successful completion of common database-editing tasks on mobile.
risks: Desktop patterns may not translate well to small screens
Adding controls could make the mobile UI feel crowded
Feature parity may not address deeper usability issues

evidence: Marketing proposes adding lightweight usage analytics to support growth experiments.
It would be useful to have basic analytics showing how often pages are viewed or edited.
Sales requests clearer workspace-level analytics to support enterprise demos.
Analytics would be more useful if they showed trends over time, not just totals.
Analytics should differentiate between viewers and editors.

insight.title: Teams need actionable usage analytics beyond aggregate totals
insight.summary: Customers and internal teams want analytics that explain how content is used over time. Viewer-editor distinctions and workspace-level trends would make the data more useful for decisions and demonstrations.
insight.recommended_action: Add trend views and role-based engagement breakdowns to workspace analytics.
insight.success_metric: Increase use of analytics views and the share of users who can answer page-engagement questions without exporting data.
risks: More metrics may increase dashboard complexity
Usage data needs clear privacy controls
Engagement measures can be misinterpreted without context
